claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has significant residual porosity.
Porosity in conventional ZrB2 is associated with reduced mechanical integrity during liquid plating-bath exposure.
A trace carbon addition can act as a reactive sintering aid for ZrB2.
The trace reactive sintering aid will enable ZrB2 sintering at approximately 2000–2100 °C.
The reactive sintering aid forms a transient liquid phase at the reduced sintering temperature.
The transient liquid phase improves particle rearrangement and packing.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport during sintering.
Improved particle rearrangement and mass transport increase densification and reduce residual porosity.
Reduced residual porosity improves the mechanical strength of ZrB2.
Reduced residual porosity decreases hole formation and eventual component failure during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
Aid-containing ZrB2 processed at 2000–2100 °C will retain a single-phase ZrB2 composition comparable to conventionally processed material.
Aid-containing, lower-temperature-processed ZrB2 will have lower porosity and greater flexural strength and fracture toughness than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Aid-containing, lower-temperature-processed ZrB2 will show less degradation and greater durability during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The preparation comparison is between conventional sintering above 2300 °C and aid-assisted sintering at approximately 2000–2100 °C.
The proposed test compares an untreated high-temperature control with a trace-carbon, lower-temperature treatment and measures phase, porosity, density, mechanical properties, and bath degradation.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in porosity, mechanical properties, and service durability, or observation of equal or greater bath degradation, would falsify the hypothesis.
